Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-18
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 53 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel, Carlos Li, Priya Narang (Redwood) — Rachel Kim, Samuel Ortiz, Benji Park, Lisa Duarte (AuroraHealth)

Summary (auto): agreed next steps to run burst tests, grant temporary telemetry access, and finalize fallback playbook; initial kernel bump improved p95 but introduced a small error burst under egress saturation.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call?
[00:05] Rachel Kim: hey Rachel here, Sam and Benji with me and Lisa, thanks Maya.
[00:10] Maya Patel: great, so agenda — quick status on ramp, Carlos will walk test findings, then fallback playbook and cutover window.
[00:18] Carlos Li: ok quick note — we ran the staged ramp from 100 req/s to 1k req/s over 30 minutes yesterday. the kernel v2.3 patch that we rolled into the Private runtime dropped p95 token latency from ~110ms to ~85ms for the 2k token profile. however, when we saturated the egress link — and i mean pushing near the 3Gbps cap on the i-ec2 limit — we saw a small error burst: about 1.8% of requests hit an application-level timeout between t+18 and t+22 minutes.
[00:38] Samuel Ortiz: wait, timeout meaning 504s? or internal retry?
[00:41] Carlos Li: mostly internal timeout — the runtime returned an internal code before we could stream tokens. it correlates with NAT translation exhaustion and TCP retransmits on the customer-side egress path.
[00:51] Benji Park: that matches what we saw in netops — our NAT pool was sized for the baseline not for the burst. we saw ephemeral port exhaustion.
[00:58] Maya Patel: mm-hmm — so two levers: we can change customer-side NAT sizing or have Redwood fallback to a smaller model variant under egress pressure. both have tradeoffs.
[01:10] Lisa Duarte: from a security perspective we prefer not to change NAT details broadly — we'd rather keep network controls. what's the fallback look like?
[01:15] Carlos Li: fallback options we sketched: 1) auto-fallback to a smaller model variant (same family, lower throughput footprint) 2) degrade batch sizes & force lower concurrent requests per connection 3) route traffic to a dedicated reserved pool in another AZ through cross-region peering as a last resort.
[01:30] Rachel Kim: cross-region peering sounds hairy with our compliance needs — could violate data residency if we fail over to a different region, right?
[01:35] Priya Narang: correct — fallback to a different region would need sign-off. we can do same-region dedicated pool first.
[01:40] Samuel Ortiz: what about static routes vs BGP? we currently use static routes in the VPC, adding BGP peering is an option but Ops will take longer to approve.
[01:48] Maya Patel: note for cutover plan we don't need BGP immediately; static route updates + pre-warmed NAT pool will likely be faster.
[01:55] Carlos Li: also worth pointing out the KV cache behavior — the kernel change improved KV cache hits on long conversation prefixes, so cost efficiency improved in steady state. but under burst the KV cache eviction rate increased due to concurrent sessions, that pushed more tokens to GPU and amplified egress bandwidth.
[02:15] Benji Park: okay — can you quantify 'amplified'?
[02:17] Carlos Li: roughly +22% additional downstream due to cache churn in that window. so if your baseline egress was 2.2Gbps we jumped to ~2.7Gbps. that nudged the NAT limits.
[02:27] Rachel Kim: good to know. so immediate mitigations?
[02:30] Maya Patel: the agreed immediate mitigations are: A) Redwood will test an automatic model-variant fallback that triggers when we see sustained connection errors for >30s during ramp B) Aurora will temporarily increase NAT port pool for the test window C) enable VPC flow logs and share them for 72 hours so both sides can correlate.
[02:48] Samuel Ortiz: we'll spin up an extra NAT gateway for the canary window; Benji will put a playbook.
[02:52] Benji Park: yep, and we'll capture sflow/netflow for the spike period.
[02:55] Carlos Li: i will also prepare a synthetic 4k-token load test that exercises prefix-heavy KV cache patterns to reproduce the eviction behavior.
[03:05] Maya Patel: excellent. now about the telemetry — Lisa, any gating on logs/flow-share?
[03:09] Lisa Duarte: we need to mask some fields, but we can provide flow logs and anonymized request IDs; we won't provide raw PII. we'll provision a short-lived role for Redwood SREs scoped to logs.
[03:19] Maya Patel: perfect, that's what we need.
[03:21] Rachel Kim: timeline for the canary cutover — thinking Friday night window to minimize user impact, but we need to align on who will be oncall.
[03:28] Maya Patel: we propose a Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC canary window; Redwood will provide one SE and one SRE standby, Aurora to provide Benji + Samuel.
[03:36] Samuel Ortiz: can do, Sunday is cleaner for our traffic.
[03:39] Carlos Li: during canary we'll run staged ramp, then a 15-minute soak at target RPS, then failover simulation where we intentionally throttle the NAT to exercise fallback. we want to observe p50/p95/p99, error rates, and KV cache churn.
[03:52] Benji Park: curious about cost — fallback to smaller model will save cost but change output fidelity. we need to validate acceptance criteria.
[03:59] Maya Patel: yes acceptance criteria: fidelity drop no more than 6% on our eval prompts, latency p95 under 150ms for 2k tokens when in fallback, and error rate <0.5% during soak.
[04:13] Rachel Kim: can you define the eval prompts? we'll share a 100-sample set by tomorrow.
[04:17] Maya Patel: perfect, share via the pilot doc link in chat.
[04:20] [00:04:20] Speaker 2: (murmur) link is in the chat as 'aurora-pilot-eval-v1'.
[04:25] Carlos Li: small note on kernel rollback — if fallback fails we'll roll the kernel to v2.2 for the dedicated pool only, not the entire fleet; that reduces risk of regressions. rollback path tested but slow — expected 10-12 minute service drain.
[04:40] Lisa Duarte: would rollback require rolling keys or anything on our side?
[04:43] Carlos Li: no key rotation. it's purely runtime binary swap; we will drain connections and bring up the older container image on the dedicated pool.
[04:49] Maya Patel: ops checklist for canary: pre-cut checklist, telemetry gating, NAT increase, model fallback enabled, rollback window, and post-cut health dashboard. we'll add specific runbook steps.
[04:58] Samuel Ortiz: for telemetry we'll need assistance correlating request IDs to flow log entries — what's the best identifier?
[05:02] Carlos Li: the best is the request_id we inject into the X-Trace header; we'll make sure the sample matches in the flow logs — we have a small script to correlate.
[05:09] Priya Narang: i'll attach that script to the pilot doc.
[05:12] Benji Park: another question — what about MTU settings? last time we saw fragmentation on certain routes that increased latency.
[05:17] Carlos Li: yeah set MTU to 9001 where possible; but if intermediate devices don't support jumbo frames we'll see fragmentation and extra packetization overhead. for the canary we'll prefer native MTU 1500 and avoid jumbo to reduce variance.
[05:30] Rachel Kim: ok that helps.
[05:33] Maya Patel: quick commercial note — there's a burst-capacity clause we can attach to the pilot so Redwood covers a portion of burst costs for two 24h windows. Maya: action item there to send.
[05:44] Rachel Kim: we'll evaluate — good faith.
[05:46] [00:05:46] Speaker 3: (unintelligible)
[05:50] Carlos Li: last technical note: during earlier test we saw a rare TLS handshake delay when the egress NAT pipeline was saturated — it manifested as a 200ms tail latency on some sessions. not common but relevant for p99.
[06:03] Benji Park: we'll capture packet captures for that interval.
[06:05] Maya Patel: ok let's recap — next steps and owners. Carlos runs synthetic load test and shares telemetry by 6/22; Benji enables VPC flow logs and provides samples by 6/19; Maya will send pilot amendment and pricing by 6/20; Rachel confirms cutover window by 6/21; Aurora to share 100-sample eval prompts by 6/19.
[06:27] Rachel Kim: sounds good. appreciate the clear plan.
[06:30] Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up in the pilot doc and schedule the Sunday canary if all aligns.
[06:35] Meeting end.
